messages:
alyssa: FYI customer reported repeated 429s during a 3-minute window this morning, claiming it looks like RPM/TPM limits even though their traffic is 'steady'. pasted sample log and headers below. can infra help confirm

mike: link to customer logs? also which API key/token are they using — user or org key?

alyssa: pasted (redacted) headers: `x-ratelimit-limit: 600`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 1680001920`. sample client metric: 9 reqs/sec sustained for 180s starting 08:12:00 UTC, then spike to ~18 reqs/sec for 20s at 08:14:40. customer insists they didn't change code.

jordan: quick checklist: 1) confirm we saw matching ingress load at edge 2) check per-key counters in rate-limiter 3) verify if any regional routing fallback or retry amplification happened. I'll start with edge logs.

sre-bot: deploy-notify: rate-limiter v2 rolled to eu-west-1 at 2024-06-05T07:55:00Z — flagged for awareness.

mike: seeing a minute-aligned burst pattern in nginx access logs from customer's IP block — these look like many short-lived HTTP clients reconnecting at minute boundaries. suspect cron-ish clients or SDK keepalive drop+reconnect.

alyssa: client claims they use our JS SDK with default retry. could retries be contributing?

jordan: yes — if retries are synchronous across workers and backoff is poor you can get retry storms. ask customer for client lib version + retry settings. meanwhile, I'll pull up token-level counters:```
# internal rate counter query
sum by (api_key) (increase(requests_total{api_key="REDACTED"}[5m]))
```

jordan: result for key RE DACTED: 1,080 requests in 5m window (avg 3.6 r/s) but note there are 2 distinct minute spikes: 08:14:00 -> 08:14:59 = ~1200 reqs and 08:20:00 -> 08:20:59 = ~900 reqs. that aligns with customer's spike windows.

priya: action items for support to ask customer: - exact SDK version + any env changes - confirm if they run cron jobs at top-of-minute - are they using multiple processes or serverless cold starts - share client-side retry/backoff settings (max retries, jitter)

mike: infra remediation ideas: - temporarily increase RPM quota for the key (if org permits) - enable short client-side 503/429 advisory header with recommended backoff - set a canary rule to smooth prefix caching for that key

alyssa: customer asked for quick mitigation; I suggested they throttle to 8 r/s and turn on exponential jittered backoff. they want us to raise quota for 15 mins while they patch. can we do temporary bump?

ops-bot: quota-change: provisional bump +50% applied to api_key=REDACTED until 1748002134 (15m). audit id=Q-202406-other

jordan: deployed a temporary per-key smoothing policy that does in-memory leaky-bucket smoothing at edge for that key; it will cap burst to 12r/s while preserving throughput. monitor logs for 10m.

mike: also found duplication: upstream proxy was retrying 3x on 502 without honoring client's idempotency key — that amplified traffic. opened ticket: infra#4521.

alyssa: customer patched client to add jitter and stagger crons. they report immediate drop in 429s after our smoothing went live.

priya: final notes to include in support reply: summary of root cause (minute-bound client spikes + retry amplification), mitigation performed (temporary quota bump, edge smoothing policy, guidance to customer), follow-ups (infra ticket for proxy retries, recommend SDK update).

mike: recommended long-term: add automatic jittered retry guidance in SDK defaults, expose token-level burst metrics in console, and add a warning when many short-lived connections are seen per key.

alyssa: thanks all — closing after customer confirms stable for 30min. :thumbsup:
